title: Frankie Trumbauer's C-melody playing
summary: Waters admires Trumbauer's tone and economical phrasing, and sings the 'Singin' the Blues' solo.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: (laughs) Oh, I told you before, I thought he was always great. I mean, I think he was, I think I've heard Benny some, I've read somethin' that Benny Carter kind of bein' a little inspired by Frankie, somethin' like - not he -

himself, not he himself, I think I've read something about it - but I thought he was playin' C melody, he wasn't playing alto like I was playin'. But his tone and his phrases, and he was playin' jazz. He just didn't make a whole lot of notes, but his
notes that he made meant something, you know. (sings "Singin' The Blues" solo)
